# just corpus: byte round-trip and token oracle, against the real core

Plan M1 acceptance: "`just corpus` passes: every corpus line round-trips byte-for-byte and its token stream
equals the `.tokens.json` oracle." Task corpus-token-oracle (M0) shipped the oracle and a structural
self-check; this task points the recipe at the real thing.

## Test shape (`crates/txtodo-core/tests/corpus.rs`, integration test → std is available)
```rust
// One #[test] per corpus file, generated by a small macro so failures name the file.
// Dev-dependency: serde + serde_json for the oracle. Core itself gains no dependency.
for entry in read_dir(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../corpus")) { … }
```
Tokens oracle entry: `{ raw, spans: [{ kind, start, end }] }`; kinds are the `TokenKind` names, so derive
`serde::Deserialize` on a test-local mirror enum, not on core's type (core stays serde-free).

## Expected strict failures (assert exactly this set, nothing else)
- every line of `lenient.txt`
- `refs.txt` bad-ref lines? No: an invalid slug is a *quirk*, not a strict error (the ABNF `tag` rule still
  matches). Strict fails only on grammar violations. So: only `lenient.txt`, plus `edge-cases.txt` line 6
  (`x 2026-09-11 (A) task`).

## Recipe (justfile is frozen; the fence asks)
```
corpus:
    .claude/scripts/check-corpus-oracle.sh
    cargo test -p txtodo-core --test corpus
```
Keep the script: it guards the oracle files themselves (contiguity, kinds) independent of the parser.
